sanskrit_verse:
भृतकस तु न कुर्वीत स्वामिनः शाट्यम अण्वपि ।
भृतिहानिमवाप्नोति ततो वादः प्रवर्तते ॥
transliteration: bhṛtakas tu na kurvīta svāminaḥ śāṭhyam aṇv api | bhṛtihānim avāpnoti tato vādaḥ pravartate ||
sph_interpretive_translation: A servant must not commit even the slightest deceit against the master; loss of wages results therefrom, and thence arises dispute.
jurisprudential_principles: Causation is traced through integrity deviation
Capacity-based responsibility requires fidelity in service
Restoration logic demands compensation aligned with capacity loss
Consciousness alignment necessitates truthfulness in relational duty
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent performs deceit against principal THEN wage entitlement is reduced proportionally to breach magnitude
IF breach causes measurable loss THEN automatic restitution protocol initiates within 24-hour period
IF dispute arises from fiduciary failure THEN mediation precedes adjudication to preserve relational dharma
IF agent demonstrates repeated deviation THEN capacity for future engagement is reviewed via integrity audit
supreme_court_application: In matters involving contractual or fiduciary relationships, the Supreme Court shall assess deviation based on svāmin-bhṛtaka dharma. The threshold of responsibility lies in demonstrable intent to deceive, regardless of outcome. Remedial action focuses on restoring relational equilibrium rather than punitive damages.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes that deceit disrupts anupūrvaśaḥ—the natural sequence of trust and performance. As śāṭya breaches svāmin-bhṛtaka alignment, proportional correction occurs through wage adjustment, not penalty. Truthful conduct is upheld as a causal prerequisite for lawful transaction.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate svāmin-bhṛtaka reconciliation dialogue within 48 hours
Implement wage recalibration reflective of integrity breach
Assign completion process requiring written reaffirmation of service ethics
Deploy consciousness realignment module to restore clarity of relational duty
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma prevails through fidelity, disputes resolve through alignment, and justice serves consciousness—not punishment.
